summary: a scientific task's tolerance by the person's standing rule, its branches in order: the reference's stated uncertainty; else the span of the quantity across suitable materials, as an acceptance interval; else the larger of half a unit in its last printed digit and the run's own numerical error, a two-grid estimate of that error entering three times over; for a reference the source gives as exact, the run's own error alone in that last branch

inputs.name: printed
inputs.meaning: the reference value as its source prints it, as text, its last digit kept as printed (a trailing zero included); in the quantity's unit; it may be null for a reference marked exact

inputs.name: stated_uncertainty
inputs.meaning: the uncertainty the source states for that value, in the quantity's unit, or null where it states none

inputs.name: run_numerical_error
inputs.meaning: the run's own numerical error of the quantity, in its unit, as an estimating skill gave it through the runner (the difference between two resolutions, or the standard error of a series the run produced); null where it was not estimated

inputs.name: run_error_from
inputs.meaning: how the run's own error was estimated: two_grids (two resolutions, as discretization_error_from_two_resolutions gives it), three_or_more_grids, or series_standard_error; null where the run's error is null

inputs.name: exact
inputs.meaning: true where the source gives the reference as exact (an analytic value of the case's own settings, a defined constant), so that it has no printed digit to be uncertain in and the half-digit branch does not apply; false or null otherwise

inputs.name: span_low
inputs.meaning: the low edge of the span of the quantity across suitable materials, in the quantity's unit, as the span's skill gave it through the runner; null where it gave none or no material was handed

inputs.name: span_high
inputs.meaning: the high edge of that span, in the quantity's unit; null where there is none

outputs.name: tolerance
outputs.meaning: the tolerance about the reference, in the quantity's unit; null where the span gave an interval in its place, and null, with why, where the inputs give none

outputs.name: interval_low
outputs.meaning: the low edge of the acceptance interval, in the quantity's unit, where the span gave it: the measured value is to lie between the two edges, the edges as handed; else null

outputs.name: interval_high
outputs.meaning: the high edge of that interval; else null

outputs.name: from
outputs.meaning: stated_uncertainty, literature_span, last_printed_digit or run_numerical_error: which of the rule's ways gave it; null where none did

outputs.name: run_error_estimated
outputs.meaning: true when a run's numerical error was handed and weighed, false when it was not estimated and the half-digit branch alone applied, null where the stated uncertainty or the span was taken

outputs.name: factor
outputs.meaning: the factor the run's own error entered with: 3 for a two-grid estimate, 1 for three or more grids or a series' standard error; null where no run error was weighed

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why no tolerance was given, or that the run's error was not estimated; else null

validity: one reference value of one quantity. The stated uncertainty, where there is one, is taken as handed: which uncertainty a source states (a standard error, the spread between its refinement levels) is the reader's to say. The last printed digit is read off the text as printed, so a trailing zero counts and a number already stored as a float has lost its printed form; an integer printed with trailing zeros is read as printed. A run's numerical error is taken as handed, with how it was estimated: estimating it is another skill's, and a run error handed without run_error_from gives no tolerance. A reference marked exact is taken as the source gives it: whether a value is exact is the reader's to say from the source, and an exact reference with no run error estimated gives no tolerance. A span is taken as handed, its two edges as the span's skill gave them: finding the materials, saying how each compares and computing the span are not this skill's, and it widens the span by nothing. A span is taken before the printed digit and the run's error whether or not the reference is marked exact, and after a stated uncertainty. It judges nothing, a tolerance the person gave overrides it, and a pass the person gave by judgement stays as it is

source.citation: the person's standing rule of 2026-11-18 (docs/ideas/20261118.md, 'Tolerances by a standing rule', amended in 'Yes, run's own error', 'Yes, factor 3', 'Yes, add literature span' and 'Min-max of values'; widened in docs/ideas/20261119.md, 'Yes, widen it'); JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM), BIPM (read 2026-11-18, https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-jcgm-100-2008-gum); NASA Glenn Research Center, NPARC Alliance CFD Verification and Validation, Examining Spatial (Grid) Convergence (read 2026-11-18, https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/wind/valid/tutorial/spatconv.html; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-nasa-grc-spatial-convergence), after P. J. Roache
source.locus: GUM F.2.2.1, The resolution of a digital indication, printed page 64: half the unit of the last printed digit is the half-width the rule takes; NASA GRC, section Grid Convergence Index (GCI): the factor of safety is recommended to be 3.0 for comparisons of two grids and 1.25 for comparisons over three or more grids; the person's rule takes the first and keeps no factor for three or more grids

Every case of v4 gives the same with the two inputs null, and says null for the two interval outputs. Common, as v4 (every simulation bundle carries it; meta_agent/tasks/025). The span of the first span case is the one literature_span@v1's first worked case gives from its materials (Schaefer and Turek 1996, V.
